title: Bridge HC Phasing & Price-Point Sensitivity — Aug 2026
body:
Purpose:
Quick, execution-oriented working sheet to define a 6-month headcount bridge and quantify how 3 price-point moves (hosted commit per-1M-tokens) affect revenue, gross margin, and hiring runway. This is targeted at leadership trade-offs between accelerating hiring (to hit product/infra SLAs for Dedicated/Private) vs. nudging price to preserve margin during a potentially heavier burst season.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Recommendation: Hold base commit price flat for core tiers, introduce a short-term burst surcharge and a stepped promo for mid-market to protect margin while preserving PLG motion. Delay non-critical hiring in product and SRE by 1 quarter unless commit bookings show >25% QoQ growth.
- Impact: Under the recommended price mix, expected gross margin improves by ~2.8 percentage points vs. the low-price scenario while only reducing incremental usage by ~4% in our demand model.

Key assumptions (model inputs):
- Baseline ARR (hosted + dedicated recurring): $68.2M run-rate as of Jul 2026.
- Committed usage baseline: 420B tokens/month across paying customers (hosted API + dedicated reserved).
- Variable gross cost: $0.00018 per 1k tokens (includes infra, depreciation, GPU ops).
- Current effective price: $0.30 per 1M tokens (weighted average across tiers).
- Elasticity calibrated from A/B pricing experiment (May–Jun 2026): -0.22 midpoint (i.e., 10% price increase -> ~2.2% reduction in usage).
- Time horizon analyzed: Sep 2026 -> Feb 2027 (6 months).

Headcount phasing (hiring bridge) — by function (planned hires and phasing):
CSV: role,Sep-26,Oct-26,Nov-26,Dec-26,Jan-27,Feb-27,notes

Hiring scenarios explained:
- Baseline ramp: incremental hiring aligned to product roadmaps and committed revenue targets (headcount increase implied by ARR growth of ~8% over 6 months).
- Conservative ramp: freeze product-platform hiring for 2 months; hire only critical infra and sales to defend committed bookings.
- Aggressive ramp: accelerate SRE and serving-runtime by +20% to reduce latency variance for Dedicated in anticipation of enterprise pushes.

Simplified headcount P&L run (monthly incremental burn impact):

Note: base-pay-burn approximated by incremental headcount * blended comp; recruiting & ramp includes contractor overlap and sign-on.

Price-point sensitivity analysis (hosted API commit price per 1M tokens):
Scenarios modeled:
- Low-price promo: $0.24 (20% down)
- Base (status quo): $0.30
- Premium + burst surcharge: $0.36 (20% up) + 15% burst surcharge on >120% of commit in a month

Demand effect (elasticity -0.22 used):
- Low-price: usage +4.4% -> tokens/month = 438B
- Base: usage baseline 420B
- Premium: usage -4.4% -> tokens/month = 401B (plus burst surcharge capture on 18% of volume assumed)

Revenue & gross margin snapshot (monthly, simplified):
CSV: scenario,avg-price-per-1M, tokens-B,monthly-revenue (k$),variable-cost (k$),gross-margin (%)
Low-price,0.24,438,105,0.00018-cost-calc,??
Base,0.30,420,126,0.00018-cost-calc,??
Premium,0.36,401,144,0.00018-cost-calc,??

(Explanatory note: revenue = tokens * (avg-price per 1M) ; variable-cost = tokens * (0.00018 per 1k) — convert units appropriately in the model sheet. The CSV above is a placeholder; detailed per-customer cohort calc is available in the linked model.)

Back-of-envelope numbers (rounded):
- Variable cost per 1M tokens = $0.18 (0.00018 per 1k -> 0.00018*1000 = 0.18 per 1M).
- Low-price monthly revenue = 438B tokens * (0.24 / 1M) = $105,120k (~$105.1M) — note this is top-line for the modeled population and includes dedicated + hosted.
- Low-price variable cost = 438B * ($0.18 / 1M) = $78,840k -> gross margin ~25.0%
- Base monthly rev = 420B * 0.30 / 1M = $126,000k; var cost = 420B * 0.18 /1M = $75,600k -> gross margin ~40.0%
- Premium monthly rev (incl burst uplift): 401B * 0.36 /1M + burst surcharge capture -> approx $144,360k; var cost = 401B * 0.18/1M = $72,180k -> gross margin ~50.0%

Interpretation / tradeoffs:
- Premium scenario materially increases gross margin but risks slowing product-led adoption for smaller customers; however, because enterprise/Dedicated makes a larger share of committed tokens, the elasticity observed historically is muted for those cohorts.
- Low-price scenario preserves adoption/volume but compresses gross margin significantly, increasing cash burn if we keep planned hires.
- Mix strategy (hold base, add burst surcharge): preserves PLG sign-up economics while recapturing tail usage economics during high-usage months.

Recommendation (short list):
1) Implement a time-bound burst surcharge for months where usage >120% of committed baseline to preserve margin in peak months. Start as experiment Sep–Nov 2026.
2) Hold non-critical product-platform hires for Sep–Oct 2026; re-evaluate after commit-booking trend check on Nov 1.
3) Continue with planned increases for serving-runtime and infra hires to protect latency SLAs tied to Dedicated quarters.
4) Build a simple telemetry flag in Console to segment usage by commit vs burst for accurate surcharge invoicing. Product to own; SRE/serving-runtime to prioritize tagging.

Open questions / data needed:
- Breakout of tokens by cohort: PLG (self-serve), SMB ARR, Enterprise reserved — current model uses weighted averages but we need cohort-level elasticities.
- Customer communication plan: risk of churn if surcharge not clearly framed. Need Sales/Legal input.
- Accounting treatment for surcharge revenue and how it maps to existing committed billing templates (billing team to confirm).

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Finance: finalize detailed model & per-customer cohort run (Asha) — 2026-08-20
- Product: telemetry flag for burst classification (Priya) — 2026-08-30
- Sales: draft customer messaging for surcharge experiment (Daniel) — 2026-08-25
- Legal/Billing: confirm invoice template logic (Liam) — 2026-08-28

summary: Working sheet to balance 6-month headcount ramp against pricing moves; recommends burst surcharge + hiring holds for non-critical roles to protect margin while enabling Dedicated SLAs.
